title: Injectivity criterion for finitely presented modules over a local essentially finitely presented algebra
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be commutative local rings, and let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism. Assume that $S$ is essentially of finite presentation over $R$, meaning that there are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $P$, a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq P$, and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong W^{-1}P$. Let $M$ and $N$ be finitely presented $S$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], let $u:M\to N$ be an $S$-linear map, assume $N$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and assume that the induced map $M/\mathfrak m_RM\to N/\mathfrak m_RN$ is injective. Then $u$ is injective and $N/u(M)$ is flat over $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), statement and proof at lines 32770--32848

proof.text: Apply simultaneous Noetherian approximation to $R\to S$, $M,N,u$. Obtain one directed system $R_i\to S_i$, modules $M_i,N_i$ and maps $u_i$, with local transitions and cocones, algebraic ring/group colimits, and the transition and limit localization and module base-change identifications. In particular both $R_i$ and $S_i$ are Noetherian, $M_i,N_i$ are finite, and every comparison carries the stage map to the later map. The approximation lemma requires neither flatness nor fibre injectivity, so all its hypotheses come directly from the statement.

source.place: Tag 046Y, first proof paragraph; Tags 00QV/00QX simultaneous presentation construction

proof.text: Apply eventual flatness with $A_i=R_i$, $B_i=S_i$ and target module $N_i$. Step 1 supplies Noetherian local stages, finite modules, local commuting transitions, the transition localizations, module base-change isomorphisms and algebraic colimits (in particular preservation of the base colimit by forgetting to sets); the limit module $N$ is $R$-flat by hypothesis. Thus some $N_{i_1}$ is $R_{i_1}$-flat. For every $j\ge i_1$, apply localized-base-change quotient flatness with $I=0$, $(R,S,R',S')=(R_{i_1},S_{i_1},R_j,S_j)$ and module $N_{i_1}$. Its conclusion, together with $N_j=N_{i_1}\otimes_{S_{i_1}}S_j$, gives $R_j$-flatness of $N_j$. Restrict to this tail; a tail of a directed set is cofinal.

source.place: Tag 046Y, first proof paragraph, invoking 00R6; Tag 00MO localized quotient flatness at I=0

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, $k_i=R_i/\mathfrak m_i$, $D_i=S_i\otimes_{R_i}k$, $P_i=M_i\otimes_{R_i}k$ and $P=M\otimes_Rk$. Locality makes $k_i\to k$ a field embedding. We have $P_i=(M_i/\mathfrak m_iM_i)\otimes_{k_i}k$, $D_i=(S_i/\mathfrak m_iS_i)\otimes_{k_i}k$ and $P=M/\mathfrak m_RM$: the identifications send $x\otimes c$ to $[x]\otimes c$ and $x\otimes[r]$ to $[rx]$. Tensor-over-quotient gives these identifications. Since $S_i$ is a localization of a finite type $R_i$-algebra, localization commuting with tensor identifies $D_i$ with a localization of a finite type $k$-algebra (base change its finitely many polynomial generators and relations). A field is Noetherian, so finite-type Noetherianity followed by localization Noetherianity makes $D_i$ Noetherian. A finite generating family of $M_i$ gives the generating family $x_a\otimes1$ of $P_i$ over $D_i$. Consequently the kernel of the $D_i$-linear comparison $\Psi_i:P_i\to P$, $x\otimes c\mapsto\mu_i(x)\otimes c$, is finite by the Noetherian submodule theorem.

source.place: Tag 046Y, middle proof paragraph, Noetherian fibre ring and finite kernel

proof.text: For $i\le j$, write $C_{ji}=S_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j$ and $S_j=W_{ji}^{-1}C_{ji}$ as in Step 1. Tensor the ring localization and the corresponding localization $M_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\to M_j$ over $R_j$ with $k$. The localization-tensor theorem identifies $D_j$ with the localization of $D_i=C_{ji}\otimes_{R_j}k$ at the image of $W_{ji}$, and identifies $P_j$ with that localization of $P_i$. These maps are the actual transitions, since their pure-tensor formulas are $s\otimes c\mapsto s_{ji}(s)\otimes c$ and $x\otimes c\mapsto m_{ji}(x)\otimes c$. Apply varying-ring tensor/colimit commutation to the system $R_i$, the modules $M_i$, and the constant additive diagram $k$ with its compatible $R_i$-actions. It gives $\varinjlim P_i=M\otimes_Rk=P$ with precisely the maps $\Psi_i$. All rings, modules and the small index set are taken in one common containing universe.

source.place: Tag 046Y, middle proof paragraph, comparison maps and localization identification; Tag 00DD tensor/colimit commutation

proof.text: Fix any index $i_0$. Step 3 makes $\ker\Psi_{i_0}$ finite over $D_{i_0}$; Step 4 supplies the localization transitions and the additive colimit required by kernel stabilization. That lemma gives $i_2\ge i_0$ for which $\Psi_j$ is injective for every $j\ge i_2$. Its finite-kernel hypothesis concerns the source module $M_j$; no injectivity assertion about a target comparison for $N_j$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 046Y, middle proof paragraph, conclusion that all sufficiently late Psi have zero kernel

proof.text: For $j\ge i_2$ set $F_j=M_j/\mathfrak m_jM_j$. The map $k_j\to k=k_j\otimes_{k_j}k$ is faithfully flat by the field-extension base-change theorem with $D=k_j$. Universal injectivity for faithfully flat maps gives an injective map $F_j\to F_j\otimes_{k_j}k$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Compose it with the injective $\Psi_j$ from Step 5. Thus the actual map $a_j:F_j\to M/\mathfrak m_RM$ is injective. In the fibre square, $b_j\overline{u_j}=\overline u\,a_j$, where $b_j:N_j/\mathfrak m_jN_j\to N/\mathfrak m_RN$ is the cocone map. If $\overline{u_j}(x)=0$, this equality and injectivity of $\overline u$ give $a_j(x)=0$, hence $x=0$. This proves injectivity of $\overline{u_j}$ without assuming $b_j$ injective.

source.place: Tag 046Y, end of middle paragraph and start of final paragraph, faithful field extension and fibre square

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian local injectivity criterion at every $j\ge i_2$ on the tail chosen in Step 2. Its base is $R_j$, its Noetherian local auxiliary ring is $S_j$, its finite source is $M_j$ and its flat $R_j$-module target is $N_j$; $u_j$ is $R_j$-linear. Step 6 supplies injectivity modulo $\mathfrak m_j$. Hence $u_j$ is injective and $C_j=N_j/u_j(M_j)$ is flat over $R_j$.

source.place: Tag 046Y, final paragraph, application of Tag 00ME

proof.text: Let $x\in M$ with $u(x)=0$. Represent $x=\mu_j(x_j)$ at a stage $j$ in the eventual-injectivity tail. Compatibility gives $\nu_j(u_j(x_j))=0$ in $N$. Apply the elementwise colimit vanishing criterion to the underlying abelian groups (equivalently $\mathbf Z$-modules): there is $l\ge j$ with $n_{lj}(u_j(x_j))=0$. This equals $u_l(m_{lj}(x_j))$, so Step 7 implies $m_{lj}(x_j)=0$ and therefore $x=0$. Thus $u$ is injective. This argument uses a later stage for each kernel element, never an identification $M_j=M$.

source.place: Tag 046Y, final sentence, injectivity of the colimit map

proof.text: Fix one $j$ in that tail. Apply tensor right exactness over $S_j$ to $M_j\xrightarrow{u_j}N_j\to C_j\to0$ and the $S_j$-algebra $S$. The compatible limit base-change identifications in Step 1 identify its first map with $u:M\to N$; hence they give a canonical isomorphism $C_j\otimes_{S_j}S\cong N/u(M)$, sending $[y]\otimes s$ to $s[\nu_j(y)]$. Apply localized-base-change quotient flatness at $I=0$ with $(R,S,R',S')=(R_j,S_j,R,S)$ and module $C_j$. Its localization hypothesis is the LIMIT localization $S_j\otimes_{R_j}R\to S$ in Step 1, and its flatness hypothesis is Step 7. Its conclusion is that $C_j\otimes_{S_j}S$ is flat over $R$. The displayed isomorphism proves the required flatness of $N/u(M)$.

source.place: Tag 046Y, final sentence, flatness of the limit cokernel; Tag 00MO at I=0
